item.title: Pentagon told Congress Iran showed no signs of attacking US first, sources say
item.description:
The United States and Israel launched a sweeping joint military offensive against Iran on February 28, 2026, striking more than 1,000 targets across the country in what the Pentagon designated Operation Epic Fury and Israel called Operation Roaring Lion. The campaign killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior officials, marking the most ambitious U.S.-Israeli military action in decades.

As operations entered their third day on Monday, the assault showed no sign of slowing, with President Donald Trump warning that strikes could continue for "four weeks or as long as necessary". The Pentagon, however, faced mounting scrutiny after administration officials acknowledged in closed-door congressional briefings that there was no intelligence suggesting Iran had planned to attack U.S. forces first.

item.title: Putin calls Gulf leaders as Iran conflict widens
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Monday to discuss the rapidly escalating military conflict in the Middle East, as the Kremlin positioned itself as a potential mediator between Tehran and the Gulf states caught in the crossfire of U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.

The call, confirmed by the UAE state news agency WAM, came as Moscow said it remained in "constant contact" with Iran's leadership and was engaged in ongoing dialogue with Persian Gulf states affected by the widening conflict.

item.title: SpaceX's Starship V3 debut slips to April as testing advances
item.description: SpaceX is in the final stages of preparing its first Starship Version 3 vehicle for flight, though the timeline for what the company calls Flight 12 appears to be shifting from a March target to no earlier than April 7, according to recent FCC filings and launch tracking data.

item.title: Bolivia raids homes to recover cash looted from deadly plane crash
item.description:
Bolivian security forces have raided at least 22 homes near the site where a military cargo plane carrying tens of millions of dollars in newly printed banknotes crashed last week, as authorities work to recover money looted from the wreckage of one of the country's deadliest aviation disasters in years.

The raids follow the February 27 crash of a Bolivian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane at El Alto International Airport, which killed at least 22 people — most of them civilians on the ground — and injured dozens more. The aircraft, arriving from Santa Cruz, was carrying 18 tons of freshly printed currency worth an estimated 423 million bolivianos, roughly $62 million, on behalf of the Central Bank of Bolivia.

item.title: Israel to reopen Kerem Shalom crossing for Gaza aid
item.description: Israel announced Monday that it will reopen the Kerem Shalom border crossing with Gaza starting Tuesday for the gradual entry of humanitarian aid, according to COGAT, the Israeli military body that oversees civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories. The decision comes after all crossings into Gaza were shut on Saturday as Israeli and U.S. forces launched joint military strikes on Iran.

item.title: Satellite images reveal vast damage to Iran's military sites
item.description:
Commercial satellite imagery collected in the days following joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran has provided an unprecedented look at the scale of destruction inflicted on military installations stretching from the country's southeastern coast to its northwestern mountains.

Images captured on March 1 and March 2 by U.S. spatial intelligence firm Vantor and Planet Labs show burning warships, collapsed tunnel entrances, obliterated drone facilities, and flattened radar systems at sites across the country. The imagery offers the clearest visual accounting yet of what American officials have described as Operation Epic Fury, launched on February 28 in coordination with Israel.

item.title: Israel launches new airstrikes on Tehran as war enters third day
item.description:
The Israeli military announced late Monday that it had begun a fresh series of airstrikes on Tehran, targeting Iranian regime installations as the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran entered its third day with no signs of abating.

The strikes followed an evacuation warning issued by the IDF's Persian-language spokesman, Lt. Col. Kamal Penhasi, urging residents in Tehran's Evin neighborhood to immediately leave areas near the headquarters of state broadcaster IRIB. Israel's Channel 12 reported that Iranian state television facilities were among the targets in the latest wave of attacks.

item.title: State Dept. tells Americans to 'depart now' from 14 Middle East nations
item.description:
The U.S. State Department on Monday issued an urgent advisory calling on American citizens to "depart now" from more than a dozen countries across the Middle East, as U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran entered their third day with no signs of slowing.

Assistant Secretary of State for Consular Affairs Mora Namdar posted the warning on X, listing Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, the West Bank and Gaza, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates, and Yemen as countries Americans should leave immediately using commercial means "due to significant safety concerns".

item.title: Antarctica lost nearly 5,000 square miles of ice in 30 years, study finds
item.description: A comprehensive 30-year satellite analysis has revealed that Antarctica's ice sheet has lost 12,820 square kilometers — nearly 5,000 square miles — of grounded ice since 1996, an area roughly equivalent to 10 cities the size of Greater Los Angeles. The findings, published Monday in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, offer the first complete mapping of Antarctica's grounding line across the entire continent over such a long time span.

item.title: Six US troops killed in Iranian strike on Kuwait base
item.description:
An Iranian strike on a makeshift military operations center at a civilian port in Kuwait has killed six American service members, marking the first US casualties since the start of Operation Epic Fury against Iran on Saturday.

The death toll climbed throughout the day Monday as military teams worked to recover remains from the burning facility. US Central Command initially reported three service members killed in action on Sunday, then confirmed a fourth had succumbed to injuries early Monday morning. By Monday afternoon, CENTCOM announced the recovery of two additional service members' remains from the struck facility, bringing the total to six killed.

item.title: Trump refuses to rule out ground troops in Iran
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Monday he would not rule out sending American ground troops into Iran, declaring that Operation Epic Fury is progressing faster than expected as the U.S. military campaign entered its third day with mounting casualties on both sides.

"I don't have the yips with respect to boots on the ground — like every president says, 'There will be no boots on the ground.' I don't say it," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published March 2. "I say 'probably don't need them,' or 'if they were necessary.'"

item.title: Rubio says Israel's strike plan triggered US attack on Iran
item.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio disclosed Monday that the United States launched its attack on Iran after learning that Israel was determined to strike with or without American participation, a revelation that cast the joint military operation in a new light and raised fresh questions about the administration's legal justification for war.

"We knew that there was going to be an Israeli action. We knew that that would precipitate an attack against American forces, and we knew that if we didn't preemptively go after them before they launched those attacks, we would suffer higher casualties," Rubio told reporters on Capitol Hill before briefing congressional leaders.

item.title: Ukraine says it recaptured more land than Russia seized in February
item.description:
Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced on March 2 that Ukrainian defense forces reclaimed more territory in February than Russian troops managed to seize — the first time Kyiv has outpaced Moscow in territorial gains since the Kursk Oblast incursion into Russian territory in the summer of 2024.

"In February 2026, for the first time since the Kursk offensive operation, the Ukrainian defence forces regained control of more territory than the enemy managed to capture," Syrskyi wrote on Telegram. "We have survived this difficult battle for winter."

item.title: Saudi Arabia goes on full military alert after Iranian drone strikes
item.description:
Saudi Arabia raised its military readiness to "full alert" on Monday after Iranian drones struck the massive Ras Tanura refinery on the kingdom's Gulf coast, as the Gulf Cooperation Council condemned Tehran's attacks across six member states and warned it reserves the right to retaliate.

The escalation came three days into a widening Middle East conflict that began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched airstrikes against Iran. Tehran responded with volleys of missiles and drones targeting GCC nations that host American military installations, killing at least six people and injuring more than 100 across the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Iranian drones strike US Embassy in Riyadh, sparking fire
item.description: A fire erupted at the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh early Tuesday after two suspected Iranian drones struck the compound, according to a U.S. State Department cable reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. There were no immediate reports of injuries, and embassy personnel sheltered in place.

item.title: Six US troops killed as Trump won't rule out ground forces in Iran
item.description:
The United States is "not currently postured" to send ground forces into Iran, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Monday, even as President Donald Trump refused to take the option off the table and the American military campaign entered its third day with mounting casualties on both sides.

Rubio, speaking on Capitol Hill before briefing the congressional "Gang of Eight," said the administration is confident its objectives can be achieved through air and naval power alone. But in comments to the New York Post, Trump struck a different tone: "Probably don't need them," he said of ground troops, adding, "if they were necessary" — a stark departure from the traditional presidential assurance of "no boots on the ground."

item.title: Trump won't rule out ground troops in Iran as strikes enter third day
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday declined to rule out deploying American ground forces to Iran, telling the New York Post he would send them "if necessary" as U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran continued into their third day under Operation Epic Fury.

"I don't have the yips with respect to boots on the ground — like every president says, 'There will be no boots on the ground.' I don't say it," Trump told the Post. "I say 'probably don't need them,' 'if they were necessary.'"

At the Pentagon, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth struck a similar tone during the first detailed briefing since the operation began on Saturday, refusing to specify what the administration would or would not do. "President Trump ensures that our enemies understand we'll go as far as we need to go to advance American interests," Hegseth said, appearing alongside Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine.

item.title: UT Austin physicists confirm 1970s 2D magnetism theory
item.description: Physicists at the University of Texas at Austin have experimentally demonstrated the full sequence of exotic magnetic phases predicted by a theoretical model of two-dimensional magnetism first proposed in the 1970s, marking the first time the complete framework has been realized in a real material. The results were published in the journal Nature Materials.

item.title: Israel's Iron Beam laser utilised in combat for first time
item.description: Israel's Iron Beam laser defense system saw its first operational use in combat early Monday as it helped intercept aerial threats launched by Hezbollah from Lebanon, marking a milestone for directed-energy weapons in warfare. The deployment came as the Middle East plunged deeper into crisis following the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in a joint U.S.-Israeli strike on February 28.

item.title: China set to lower growth target as parliament opens
item.description: China is poised to trim its economic growth target for the first time in four years when Premier Li Qiang delivers the government work report at the opening of the National People's Congress on March 5. Most analysts expect Beijing to set a 2026 GDP growth target of 4.5% to 5%, a step down from the "around 5%" goal maintained over the past three years.
